subject: RFI: Dedicated capacity & burst profile for EdgeScale
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@edgescale.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@edgescale.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: Dedicated capacity & burst profile for EdgeScale

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the call earlier. As discussed, we're preparing an RFP to firm up reserved capacity for our inference pairs in H1 2027. Our immediate goal is to size a commitment that covers steady-state traffic while allowing predictable bursts (up to 3x for 30–90s) during batch scoring windows and weekly peak reports.

I've attached a small sample of our workload traces (edgescale_workload_samples.csv). Key asks we need in the RFI response:
- Recommended GPU instance types and mix for the steady vs burst profiles
- Expected sustained throughput (tokens/sec) per GPU by model family (Llama2-70B, Mistral-8x40B equivalent)
- Reservation billing model (how burst/overage is handled and estimated cost)
- Recovery SLA and fallback model when reservation capacity is exhausted

Can you send a short worksheet and a pricing sketch that maps our steady vs preferred burst targets to a reservation commitment? We need this to complete procurement sign-off next week.

Best,
Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of IT Infrastructure, EdgeScale
(t.ellis@edgescale.ai)

---
Attachment: edgescale_workload_samples.csv (CSV, 42 KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@edgescale.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity & burst profile for EdgeScale

Tom — thanks for the trace and clear asks. I've looped in Karthik (dedicated capacity engineering) and Rishi (pricing & commercial). We're attaching a compact worksheet (redwood_capacity_pricing_v2.xlsx) and a short burst-profile diagram that maps steady-state vs 3x bursts to reservation sizing.

High level summary up front:
- Recommended baseline: 8 x A800-equivalent GPUs (mixed 2x A100-80GB-equivalent for high-memory Llama2-70B and 6x A800 for throughput-efficient runs). That maps to an estimated baseline aggregate throughput of ~18k tokens/sec for your mix when using Redwood continuous batching and KV-prefix cache.
- Burst strategy: reserve an additional 4x A800 as burst capacity (pre-warmed in a burst pool with fast warm-start). That provides ~3x headroom for short windows while keeping average committed footprint lower.
- Overage/fallback: real-time routing will spill to hosted surplus capacity if reservations are saturated; overage is billed at a pre-agreed premium rate or can be offset by auto-scaling credits in the contract.
- SLA & recovery: targeted 99.9% availability on reserved pool; fallbacks to compatible quantized model variants with SLO on correctness degradation documented.

Notes on assumptions included in the worksheet: tokenization ratio (avg 4 chars/token), median sequence length (32), percentage of cached prefixes (25%) during burst windows. Karthik and I added conservative warm-up (30s) for cold KV caches.

We'll highlight cost tradeoffs by giving two commitment tiers in the worksheet ("Conservative" and "Aggressive") and show expected monthly spend with burst usage patterns.

Next steps: if that sounds reasonable we'll schedule a 30-min walk-through of the worksheet with your procurement team. Can you do Thu 12/03 or Mon 12/07 in the morning PT?

Regards,
Priyom Das
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
(priyom_das@redwood.com)

Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity & burst profile for EdgeScale

Tom / Priyom — quick technical add from the infra side. A few clarifications so our sizing matches what you run in prod: 

1) Models: please confirm whether you will run Llama2-70B in fp16 or an int8 quantized variant in production. Our throughput per GPU varies ~1.8–2.2x between those modes.
2) KV cache hit assumptions: your trace shows many repeated conversational prefixes; if you can confirm a 30% prefix-hit rate our steady-state GPUs can sustain higher effective throughput without increasing reservations.
3) Persistent vs ephemeral burst: if bursts are predictable (scheduled daily) we can recommend keeping small dedicated burst pool always warm; for fully ad-hoc bursts, we propose a hybrid approach with fast-hosted fallback and a lower-priced overage band.

Technical numbers we used in the worksheet (conservative):
- A100-80GB equiv: ~2.2k tokens/sec for L70B fp16; ~3.8k tokens/sec if running int8-quantized variants with Redwood optimizations.
- A800 equiv: ~2.6k tokens/sec int8 (throughput-optimized kernels).

If you confirm model quantization and an expected prefix-hit %, we'll re-run the worksheet and provide a final committed GPU mix and monthly cost ranges.

-Karthik
Senior Staff Engineer, Dedicated Runtime
Redwood Inference
(karthik_iyer@redwood.com)

- Bursts are semi-predictable: we schedule major batch scoring Tues/Thu 04:00 PT for 10–15 minutes, and an ad-hoc daily reporting burst of ~60–90s.
